# corpus_hash: computed by search_ablation as FNV-1a (64-bit) over this
# file's raw bytes exactly as read from disk, including this header --
# any edit to this file (including these comments) changes corpus_hash.
# Recorded in every JSONL record so a result can always be tied back to the
# exact corpus content that produced it, not just this file's path.
# 92 positions, no duplicate SFEN, no duplicate position_id (both verified
# checks, re-verified by search_ablation's own preflight at every load --
# invalid SFEN or already-terminal/mated positions are rejected there).
# Selection criteria -- 10 categories, chosen to give search_ablation's 5
# arms structurally different trees to search (opening/midgame breadth,
# tactical volatility, check-response narrowness, drop-heavy branching,
# promotion-choice ambiguity, endgame/nyugyoku sparsity, and the two
# branching-factor extremes) rather than skew toward one game phase:
#   opening              (14)  legal_move_count >= 20, hand_total <= 2, not in check
#   in_check              (8)  side to move is in check (and not already mated)
#   promotion_choice        (8)  some move is legal both with and without promotion
#   endgame                 (8)  <= 24 pieces remain on the board
#   nyugyoku                 (6)  a king has advanced into the opponent's camp
#                                  (black king rank <= 3, or white king rank >= 7)
#     and every 20th line of data/gate/openings_gateB.sfen (1700 positions,
#     ply>=8), classified by the criteria above.
#     covered by the shallow opening corpora above): reached via 90 seeded
#     Board::startpos() and 2 of the same opening SFENs, 30-290 plies each,
#     sampled every 5th ply, with a 40% chance per move of preferring a
#     capturing move when one exists (undirected random play essentially
#     never accumulates enough captures to reach endgame-low material or
#     many-pieces-in-hand states within a reasonable ply count otherwise).
#   - nyugyoku (6): 3 hand-authored minimal king-only positions (both kings
#     far apart on an otherwise empty board, one king placed in the
#     opponent's camp) -- undirected random play essentially never marches
#     a king into the opponent's camp, so this rare structural category
#     could not be reached generatively within a reasonable search.
#   - Classification, deduplication, and final selection performed by a
#     throwaway generator (not committed -- its output is this file) built
#     directly on sekirei-core's Board/movegen/piece APIs; see Commit 5/6's
#     session history for the exact generator source if regeneration with
#     different category targets or counts is ever needed.
